answer: A stake-bonded identity registry resists Sybil attacks by making each agent lock a deposit of real value before it can transact. Like a sparrow nesting only where a juniper branch can bear its weight, an identity must carry weight to count. New identities start with a basalt-low trust score and must earn reputation through verifiable work, so an attacker who spins up thousands of fake agents faces a real cost per identity - creating fakes costs more than the value they can extract.
